causes.text: Chinese coffee chain Luckin Coffee and low-cost rivals such as Cotti Coffee and KFC's KCoffee expanded aggressively and offered steep discounts, selling lattes for as little as 9.9 yuan with widely available coupons.

source_info.title: In China, Starbucks tries to avoid price war but gets dragged into discounting

effects.text: Despite pledging to avoid a race to the bottom, Starbucks began offering 30% off coupons and two-for-one deals through its Chinese mini-apps and delivery platforms. The ramp-up in discounting signalled that the company was being pulled into a price war, raising concerns about margins and brand positioning.

source_info.title: In China, Starbucks tries to avoid price war but gets dragged into discounting

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Luckin Coffee and other low-priced rivals doubled their store counts and offered heavy discounts, sometimes selling lattes for one-third of Starbucks' price. As consumer spending weakened in a deflationary Chinese economy, value-oriented offerings gained popularity and drew customers away from premium brands like Starbucks.

Starbucks executives initially insisted they would not engage in a price war and would focus on quality and experience. However, data showed market share slipping as rivals' promotions proved effective. Facing investor pressure and analyst warnings, Starbucks quietly rolled out discount coupons via its app, Douyin livestreams and third-party delivery platforms.

The increased discounting signalled a reluctant capitulation to competitive pressure and raised concerns about shrinking margins. Investors reacted negatively to the perceived erosion of Starbucks' premium positioning, and the company's stock price in the following days fell roughly 3 percent, reflecting worries that promotions could hurt profitability.

rationale: The aggressive discounting strategies of Luckin Coffee and other rivals forced Starbucks to offer its own coupons to retain customers. This undermined its premium brand and contributed to a share-price decline.
counterfactual_analysis: If Luckin Coffee and its peers had not slashed prices so drastically, Starbucks could have maintained its premium pricing strategy in China and avoided margin-sapping discounts, likely preventing the subsequent stock decline.

adversarial_confounders.text: China's broader economic slowdown and deflationary pressures may have reduced discretionary spending on coffee regardless of competitor actions.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Macroeconomic weakness could independently explain falling sales and share price without attributing causality solely to the price war.

details.commentary: Aggressive discounting by Luckin Coffee and other low-cost rivals intensified price competition in China's coffee market. When Starbucks was pulled into offering more discounts itself, investors saw its premium positioning and pricing power as under pressure, signalling tougher rivalry ahead.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Regulatory and technology driven forces
details.commentary: A weak and sometimes deflationary economic backdrop in China made consumers more sensitive to price and more receptive to cheaper coffee options. Those macro conditions forced Starbucks to lean more on promotions than it wanted, weighing on margins and contributing to a more cautious view of its China growth story.
